gina_krog.name: Gina Krog
gina_krog.notes: Rich gas by its own 20-inch line to Sleipner A (SODIR pipeline register). Capacity: the highest month of SODIR net gas, Sep 2024 to Aug 2026; position: SODIR facility register

ivar_aasen.name: Ivar Aasen
ivar_aasen.notes: Oil and gas to the Edvard Grieg platform for processing, gas on through the Utsira High line to SAGE. Capacity: the highest month of SODIR net gas, Sep 2024 to Aug 2026

dvalin.name: Dvalin
dvalin.notes: Subsea field; the well stream goes to Heidrun's dedicated Dvalin gas module, and the gas is exported via Polarled to Nyhamna. Capacity: the highest month of SODIR net gas, Sep 2024 to Aug 2026

dvalin_tee.name: Dvalin tie-in (Polarled)
dvalin_tee.notes: DVALIN PLEM in SODIR's facility register, on the Polarled route: where Dvalin's gas from Heidrun joins Polarled

valhall.name: Valhall
valhall.notes: Gas is sent via Norpipe to Emden; oil and NGL go to the Ekofisk Centre. Includes Hod, processed on Valhall. Capacity: the highest month of SODIR net gas (Valhall plus Hod), Sep 2024 to Aug 2026; position: Valhall PH

jotun.name: Jotun FPSO (Balder area)
jotun.notes: The Jotun FPSO processes Ringhorne and excess Balder gas and exports rich gas via Statpipe (norskpetroleum.no, Jotun and Balder). Capacity: the highest month of SODIR net gas from Balder and Jotun, Sep 2024 to Aug 2026

jotun_tee.name: Jotun tie-in (Statpipe)
jotun_tee.notes: JOTUN T in SODIR's facility register (Statpipe): on Heimskringla's Draupner leg, about 11 km south of the Heimskringla T

martin_linge.name: Martin Linge
martin_linge.notes: Rich gas to the Frigg UK pipeline (FUKA) and on to the SEGAL terminal at St Fergus. Capacity: the highest month of SODIR net gas, Sep 2024 to Aug 2026

fuka_tee.name: FUKA tie-in (Frigg TP1)
fuka_tee.notes: FRIGG TP1-Y in SODIR's facility register: the end of the Martin Linge gas line, where it joins the Frigg UK System (FUKA) at the old Frigg TP1 bypass

mariner.name: Mariner
mariner.notes: UK heavy-oil field (first oil August 2019; operated by Adura since 1 Dec 2025, https://www.equinor.com/energy/mariner). It takes gas: a 6-inch, 33 km import line from a tee on Vesterled (NSTA PL3768) feeds its power generation. No supply in the model and not an exit

mariner_tee.name: Mariner tie-in (Vesterled)
mariner_tee.notes: NSTA PL3917, the Mariner spool at the Vesterled tee: where Mariner's gas import line leaves Heimskringla's St Fergus leg

grane.name: Grane
grane.notes: Oil field that takes gas for injection through the 18-inch Grane gas pipeline from the Heimdal riser (SODIR pipeline register, in service). SODIR records no net gas sales from Grane (Sep 2024 to Aug 2026), so it is no supply in the model and not an exit; oil goes to Sture

ivar_aasen_edvard_grieg.notes: Oil and gas to Edvard Grieg for processing; a field line, not in SODIR's transport register, so drawn straight

dvalin_gas.name: Dvalin gas export (via Heidrun)
dvalin_gas.notes: Well stream to Heidrun's Dvalin gas module, then gas from the Dvalin gas export riser base at Heidrun to the Dvalin PLEM on Polarled (SODIR facility register). One row, so Heidrun's own gas keeps to Haltenpipe and Åsgard Transport

valhall_norpipe.name: Valhall gas export
valhall_norpipe.notes: Gas is sent via Norpipe to Emden (norskpetroleum.no; Wikipedia: "transported directly via the Norpipe pipeline", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valhall_oil_field). The tie-in point is not in SODIR's transport register: drawn into the Norpipe tie-in, as on Gassco's schematic

jotun_gas.name: Jotun gas export
jotun_gas.notes: Rich gas from the Jotun FPSO into Statpipe at Jotun T (SODIR facility register); a field line, not in the transport register, so drawn straight

heimskringla_jotun.notes: From the T to the Jotun tie-in; split from the Draupner leg (was the Heimdal leg of Statpipe)

martin_linge_gas.name: Martin Linge gas pipeline

fuka.name: Frigg UK System (FUKA)
fuka.notes: NSTA PL6N, PL2026 and PL6S: 32-inch, from the Frigg TP1 subsea bypass to the St Fergus gas plant (175 + 2 + 186 km). It lands at SEGAL (https://www.norskpetroleum.no/en/facts/field/martin-linge/); its UK feeders (Alwyn and others) are not modelled

mariner_gas_import.name: Mariner gas import

grane_gas_import.name: Grane gas pipeline
grane_gas_import.notes: 18-inch line from the Heimdal riser to Grane, gas for injection (SODIR pipeline register, in service). No exit in the model, so the routing sends none

streams.name: denmark-gas-energinet
streams.title: Danish gas flows, Aug to Oct 2026
streams.description: Measured daily flows through the Danish gas system from Energinet: gas arriving from the North Sea (mostly Norwegian gas through Baltic Pipe) and the onward flow to Poland. Real data for two pipelines; the rest of the chart has no readings.
streams.license: Open data from Energinet's Energi Data Service; credit Energinet as the source

streams.name: norway-exports
streams.title: Norwegian gas landings on the continent, hourly, Oct 2026
streams.description: Hourly physical flows where Norwegian gas lands on the continent, 13 to 20 Oct 2026, as the receiving operators report them to the ENTSOG Transparency Platform: Dunkerque (Franpipe), Zeebrugge ZPT (Zeepipe I), Dornum (Europipe II), Emden EPT1 (Europipe I and Norpipe together: the operators have metered them as one point since Oct 2015, so the reading is on the Emden terminal, not split between the two lines) and Baltic Pipe's North Sea Entry into Denmark. The UK publishes daily values only: Easington is in the norway-exports-daily dataset, and St Fergus mixes Norwegian and UK gas, so Vesterled, FLAGS and SAGE have no readings here.
streams.license: ENTSOG Transparency Platform terms of use; credit ENTSOG as the source

streams.name: norway-exports-daily
streams.title: Norwegian gas landings, daily, Oct 2026
streams.description: Daily physical flows at the points where Norwegian gas lands, 1 to 28 Oct 2026, from the ENTSOG Transparency Platform: the continental points of the hourly norway-exports dataset plus Easington (Langeled), which National Gas reports per gas day only. Each reading is the gas day's flow, shown at the start of the gas day (06:00 CET). St Fergus mixes Norwegian and UK gas (its flow is above what Vesterled can carry), so Vesterled, FLAGS and SAGE have no readings. Emden EPT1 is Europipe I and Norpipe together, read on the Emden terminal.
streams.license: ENTSOG Transparency Platform terms of use; credit ENTSOG as the source

streams.name: sodir-field-production
streams.title: Norwegian field production, Sep 2024 to Aug 2026
streams.description: Monthly net gas produced by Norwegian offshore fields, from the Norwegian Offshore Directorate (SODIR) factpages. Real monthly averages for the fields NORA models; Sleipner Vest and Øst are summed into the Sleipner node, Valhall and Hod into Valhall, and Balder and Jotun into the Jotun FPSO. The rest of the chart has no readings.
streams.license: Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD), https://data.norge.no/nlod/en; credit SODIR as the source

sources.units.toml:
# Units for level 2 (unit control): each groups the assets one operator desk looks after.
# Every node belongs to exactly one unit; a pipeline belongs to the unit it leaves from.
# Order here is the order on screen. `nora validate` checks every id.

[units.norwegian_sea]
name = "Norwegian Sea"
nodes = [
    "aasta_hansteen", "norne", "heidrun", "asgard", "smorbukk_nord", "mikkel", "morvin",
    "trestakk", "skarv", "aerfugl", "draugen", "ormen_lange", "nyhamna", "tjeldbergodden",
    "dvalin", "dvalin_tee",
]

[units.northern_north_sea]
name = "Northern North Sea"
nodes = [
    "gjoa", "visund", "statfjord", "gullfaks", "tordis", "gullfaks_sor", "flags_brent", "kvitebjorn", "troll",
    "oseberg", "kollsnes", "heimdal", "beryl", "edvard_grieg", "frigg", "odin", "ivar_aasen",
    "martin_linge", "fuka_tee", "mariner", "mariner_tee", "grane", "jotun", "jotun_tee",
]

[units.hubs]
name = "Kårstø, Sleipner and Draupner"
nodes = [
    "karsto", "johan_sverdrup", "gudrun", "gina_krog", "sleipner", "draupner_s", "draupner_e",
    "ekofisk", "ekofisk_tee", "valhall",
]

[units.uk]
name = "UK landings"
nodes = ["st_fergus", "easington"]

[units.continent]
name = "Continental landings"
nodes = ["dornum", "emden", "zeebrugge", "dunkirk"]

[units.denmark_poland]
name = "Denmark and Poland"
nodes = ["baltic_tie", "nybro", "pl_vtp"]
sources.flow_layout.toml:
# Where each node sits in the Flow view: [across, down] in grid steps (one step across
# is one square's width with room; one step down is one row of squares with names).
# Laid out after the operators' Area D screen (Ray, 29 Oct: "position the nodes better,
# you already got an image from me"): the fields across the top from Gjøa and Statfjord
# to Heidrun and Norne, St Fergus and the UK on the left, Nyhamna and Kollsnes in the
# middle, Kårstø on the right, Sleipner, Draupner S and E across the middle, the landings
# along the bottom from west to east. No line runs through another node. Drag a node in the Flow view and
# Save. A node not listed here is placed by layout.py. `nora validate` checks the ids.
# Gassco's schematic (issue #38) adds Martin Linge on FUKA, Dvalin on Polarled, the
# Jotun and Mariner tie-ins on Heimskringla, Grane, Ivar Aasen, Gina Krog and Valhall;
# the rows from St Fergus down moved lower to make room for them.

[positions]
# fields across the top, west to east
martin_linge = [-1.0, 0]
gjoa = [0, 0]
statfjord = [2.0, 0.55]
gullfaks = [3.0, 0]
oseberg = [4.2, 0]
ormen_lange = [5.6, 0]
aasta_hansteen = [6.6, 0]
dvalin = [7.6, 0]
troll = [8.6, 0]
kvitebjorn = [9.6, 0]
visund = [10.8, 0]
heidrun = [14.6, 0]  # at the right end: Haltenpipe runs down the edge to Tjeldbergodden
norne = [13.4, 0]
# St Fergus and the UK, the processing plants, Kårstø and the Norwegian Sea
fuka_tee = [-1.0, 1.4]  # where Martin Linge's line joins FUKA (Frigg TP1)
flags_brent = [0.3, 1.0]
beryl = [1.3, 1.6]
edvard_grieg = [2.3, 1.55]
ivar_aasen = [3.3, 1.1]
st_fergus = [0, 2.75]
mariner_tee = [1.8, 2.72]  # on Heimskringla's St Fergus leg
mariner = [1.6, 3.8]  # takes gas from the tie-in
heimdal = [3.4, 2.7]  # the Heimskringla T (Ray, 29 Oct)
grane = [4.4, 2.3]  # takes gas from the T
jotun = [5.4, 2.8]
jotun_tee = [5.0, 4.0]  # on Heimskringla's Draupner leg
nyhamna = [6.2, 1.45]
dvalin_tee = [7.2, 1.55]  # on Polarled
kollsnes = [9.0, 1.8]
asgard = [13.6, 1.0]
karsto = [12.6, 1.75]
johan_sverdrup = [11.3, 3.1]
# the hubs, Ekofisk and the southern fields
sleipner = [2.6, 4.5]
gudrun = [1.2, 4.8]
gina_krog = [2.3, 5.5]
draupner_s = [6.6, 4.5]
draupner_e = [8.8, 4.5]
ekofisk = [5.4, 5.15]
valhall = [6.4, 5.9]
ekofisk_tee = [7.4, 5.7]  # on the line from Draupner S to Emden (Area D)
baltic_tie = [12.6, 5.1]
# the exit points along the bottom, west to east; St Fergus and Nyhamna stay where their
# lines are (Ray, 30 Oct: "all exit points except nyhamna and st.fergus should be lined at
# the bottom of the flow view, we need it to look orderly and nice")
easington = [0.2, 7.0]
dunkirk = [1.6, 7.0]
zeebrugge = [3.2, 7.0]
emden = [10.2, 7.0]
dornum = [12.6, 7.0]
